| [LIT-001](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-001.md) v2 | Quantum Mechanics can be understood through stochastic optimization on spacetimes | Lindgren & Liukkonen (2019), DOI-10.1038/s41598-019-56357-3. The paper derives a Stueckelberg-type equation i∂φ/∂τ = (1/2m)□φ − Vφ (Eq. 36) from an HJB equation, but only after putting the imaginary unit in twice by hand. The first i is a factor √g = i multiplying the Lagrangian; standard relativity uses √(−g) = 1. The second is a complex "variance" σ² = i/m (Eq. 29), chosen so that the Hopf–Cole substitution J = log φ linearizes the equation. The linearization itself is the standard λ = σ²·(control cost) condition. The Schrödinger equation (Eq. 43) then comes from c → ∞ plus complex conjugation. The Dirac equation is not derived, and the "Klein–Gordon equation" (Eq. 40) has 2mV where m² should be. | Rejected — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-003](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-003.md)); the claim that the i comes from the Minkowski metric depends on the non-standard √g, not √(−g). | [LIT-019](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-019.md) v2 | Why interference phenomena do not capture the essence of quantum theory | Catani et al. (2021), [ARXIV-2111.13727](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.13727). The paper models each mode of the interferometer as a classical bit pair (occupation N ∈ Z_2, phase Φ ∈ Z_2). The agent may know only one of N, Φ or N⊕Φ and must be maximally ignorant of the rest. Under that restriction, local and deterministic dynamics (beamsplitter: swap N_L with Φ_L⊕Φ_R) reproduce exactly the 50-50, ϕ ∈ {0, π} Mach–Zehnder statistics (output port L with probability 1 or 0; ½/½ with a which-way detector). The same holds for the Elitzur–Vaidman bomb tester (success probability ¼), delayed choice and the quantum eraser (interference within each P_A outcome class, none within each Q_A class). So this "TRAP" slice of interference phenomenology cannot, on its own, force wave–particle complementarity, observer-dependence or nonlocal/retrocausal influence. The paper leaves aside the phenomenology it concedes is nonclassical (unbalanced beamsplitters, the functional form of the duality relation, Hardy's interferometer). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 (NOTE-018); It is the worked, experiment-by-experiment defence of placing interference in the weakly nonclassical column of LIT-007's Table II, and it has the clearest statement of the Spekkens-school methodology (define classicality, formalize it, prove a no-go). | [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md) v2 | The Homological Nature of Entropy | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), DOI-10.3390/e17053253. On a finite probability space, take an information structure S (a set of partitions closed under joins that have a common refinement in S and containing the trivial partition) and a probability family Q complete for it. The information cohomology H*(S;Q) is computed by a Hochschild-type bar complex whose action is Shannon's averaged conditioning. If S is connected and "sufficiently rich" and cochains are measurable, then H¹ is one-dimensional and spanned by Shannon entropy (Thm 1). This makes entropy the unique measurable 1-cocycle, up to one multiplicative constant per connected component. In the unitary-invariant quantum case H¹_U = 0: Shannon entropy is the coboundary of minus the von Neumann entropy, which is the unique invariant 0-cochain with that property up to an additive constant (Thm 3). The tree ("arborescent") version again gives H¹ spanned by entropy (Thm 4). | Active — read in full 2026-09-25 ([NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md)); the founding paper of information cohomology, with complete proofs of the degree-one results (Thms 1, 3, 4). Read it for those. Its broader programme (higher mutual informations as cocycles, super/sub-harmonicity, max-entropy discrimination) is sketched or deferred here to unpublished companion papers. |

The paper argues, with no new theorem, that the Lombardi–da Costa ontology of properties for quantum mechanics can be stated in Krause's quasi-set theory Q. On that ontology a system is a bundle of I-type-properties (instances of universal type-properties, represented by the algebra of observables) with no principle of individuality. For each property instance, the indiscernible instances form a qset U([Π]). An atomic bundle is any qset x with qc(x ∩ U) = 1 for each U; the Axiom of Choice in Q guarantees one exists. The bundle's kind is Q(B) = {x ∈ P(Q) \| R(x)}, whose members are all indiscernible. N particles are a subqset N(B) ⊂ Q(B) with qc = N, a definite number with no labels (§6, pp. 19–22). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-127.md)); worth reading as a short, clear bridge between the modal-Hamiltonian "ontology of properties" (Lombardi et al.) and quasi-set theory (French & Krause 2006). | [LIT-121](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-121.md) v2 | The Meaning of the Wave Function: In Search of the Ontology of Quantum Mechanics | Gao (2016), [ARXIV-1611.02738](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02738). Gao argues first that ψ is real. His case uses protective measurements, which yield ⟨A⟩ on a single system with certainty, in three versions (ch. 4): one in the ontological-models framework using preparation non-contextuality, two he says need no auxiliary assumption, and one that uses a new criterion of reality. He then argues that ψ describes random discontinuous motion (RDM) of N point particles in 3-space: \|ψ\|² is the density with which each particle is present at each instant, and ψ is a single-case propensity. The main support is that the charge density \|ψ\|²Q, which protective measurement shows to exist, has no self-interaction (chs. 6–7). If the Born probabilities come from RDM, collapse is real. Gao proposes an energy-conserving, Planck-time-discrete collapse model: Pᵢ(t+t_P) = Pᵢ(t) + (ΔE/E_P)[δ_{EsEi} − Pᵢ(t)], giving τ_c ≈ ħE_P/(ΔE)² (ch. 8). Combined with relativity, it requires a detectable preferred Lorentz frame (ch. 9). | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-140); worth reading as the fullest single statement of the protective-measurement argument for ψ-reality and of the RDM ontology. Its chapters 2, 3, 7.1 and 8.5 are also a well-referenced critical survey of ψ-epistemic, nomological, configuration-space-realist, Penrose and CSL views. Its central premises are contested (see Limitations), its collapse model is unconfirmed, and chapters 8–9 are openly speculative. |

A programmatic essay, not a result paper. Carroll argues that a quantum theory is fixed, up to unitary equivalence, by the Hamiltonian's eigenvalue list {E_n} on a finite-dimensional factor (he assumes a non-degenerate spectrum), and that parts are not given. Subsystems (tensor factorisations H = H_S ⊗ H_E or ⨂_α H_α), classicality and space are to be selected afterwards as rare structure that suits the dynamics. The only uniqueness he reports is for local factorisations, and it rests on a cited theorem (Cotler et al. 2019). The system/environment criterion rests on "simple numerical examples" in a companion paper, the metric and Einstein's equation on "optimistic assumptions", and emergent fields on a hope. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-134); worth reading as the shortest authoritative statement of Hilbert-space fundamentalism and its "quantum mereology" programme, with the caution that nothing is derived in it. A reader wanting minimal observers or agents is better served by the sources it surveys: Ashby, Hartle's IGUS, Fields, and Gielen & Wise's observer space in §4.10.3. |

A closure principle has two tacit parameters, its domain and its completeness relation (causal, dynamical or explanatory). Wave-function realism falsifies spatiotemporal-domain closure (STC) but is compatible with fundamental-physical closure (FPC), so there is no "trans-domain causal breach". The physicalist is left with a dilemma: STC is too narrow, and FPC needs an independent criterion of physicality plus a dynamical-to-causal bridge. The paper tests this across primitive-ontology, spacetime-state, multi-field, Everettian, nomological and dispositional readings. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md)); worth reading as the clearest statement of what quantum ontology does and does not do to causal-closure arguments. French answers Howard's objection that QFT's unitarily inequivalent representations leave the structural realist with non-isomorphic, competing structures. He offers two routes. The first is to adopt cut-off "conventional" QFT with Wallace, on which the inequivalence is an artefact or harmless. The second is to follow Ruetsche's Swiss Army Knife and treat the algebra as a modal structure spanning all representations. On that reading spontaneous symmetry breaking preserves the symmetry across the degenerate vacua, and the DHR analysis derives quantum statistics from the algebra. Adding Baker's criterion, on which a symmetry mapping between representations suffices for intertranslatability, removes the assumption behind the objection, and French ends with a third option that combines the two routes. Every step is an informal argument layered on others' technical results; the paper proves nothing itself. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md)); worth reading as a leading ontic structural realist's worked response to the strongest physics-based objection to OSR beyond finite-dimensional QM, and for its clear staging of the Wallace–Fraser and algebraic versus Hilbert-space debates. Morganti argues from a survey rather than proving anything. What OSR gets right about symmetry, entanglement and particle kinds is better captured by "metaphysical coherentism": object-like entities (in one domain) stand in symmetric *partial* ontological dependence on one another. Cycles of such dependence can be kept irreflexive, and so explanatorily non-trivial, by relaxing transitivity (quasi-transitivity) or by making only partial dependence symmetric. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-095](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-095.md)); worth reading as the clearest statement of a dependence-based, object-friendly alternative to relation-first OSR, and a hub for the grounding, holism and OSR literatures; its physics applications are programmatic, and he says so himself (pp. 18–19). |

An event reading fits GRW flashes, GRW matter density and Bohmian worldlines, and also the antirealist views of ψ held by Bohr, Rovelli, Haag and Pashby. Because it is the same across interpretations, he calls it "interpretation-independent" (p. 12). Where ψ needs a realist reading, it should be read as intrinsic dispositions of events. Esfeld et al.'s view has the opposite structure: bare matter points plus a single holistic power of the universal configuration. Rovelli restates RQM as an ontology of sparse relative facts, which arise in interactions and are labelled by the interacting systems. Its one technical rule is that an amplitude W(b,a) gives the probability P = \|W\|² only when a and b are relative to the same system. That rule removes the clash between P_collapse = Σᵢ\|W(c,bᵢ)\|²\|W(bᵢ,a)\|² and P_unitary = \|ΣᵢW(c,bᵢ)W(bᵢ,a)\|² (eqs. 2–4). The book gives a formal Schema: a duality is an isomorphism between the "model roots" (state space, quantities, dynamics) of two models of a common-core bare theory, with values and dynamics matching. It pairs this with an interpretative condition: duals are physically equivalent iff (A) they are duals and (B) i1 = i2∘d. On that basis it argues four things. First, there are no genuine cases of in-principle underdetermination in the examples, and a cautious realist can commit to the common core. Second, dualities do not favour structural realism. Fourth, quasi-dualities motivate a "geometric view" on which models are charts on a successor theory's moduli space. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 (NOTE-178); worth reading as the reference treatment of dualities in philosophy of physics. On this view it is an ingredient that "partially realizes" the law, not a law and not a material field. So its time-dependence and non-uniqueness (a phase shift, a density matrix) are harmless, it counts as non-epistemic and ontic, and it can take part in constructive explanation. Each of these is argued informally, and the escape from PBR is by relabelling the ontic/epistemic distinction, not by engaging the theorem. | Proposed — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-154.md)); a distinct and clearly placed option in the ψ-as-law family ([LIT-204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-204.md) §4.2). The book recasts IR's vector-space, probabilistic and logical models in one Hilbert-space language. Documents are state vectors. Relevance and aboutness are Hermitian observables that need not commute. Subspaces carry a non-distributive logic whose conditional is shown to be a Stalnaker conditional equal to the Sasaki hook (ch. 5). Gleason's theorem makes tr(ρP) the probability of a subspace, which ch. 6 uses to rewrite cosine matching, cluster representatives, relevance and pseudo-relevance feedback, dynamic clustering and ostensive retrieval. | [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) v2 | Measurement as Sheafification: Context, Logic, and Truth after Quantum Mechanics | Ghose (2025), [ARXIV-2512.12249](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12249). A programmatic essay, with no theorem, model or computation of its own. It restates Abramsky & Brandenburger's criterion (contextuality and non-locality as the absence of a global section of a presheaf over measurement contexts) and adds three things. It declares measurement to be "sheafification" of that presheaf, without specifying a site, a topology or any sheafified object. It asserts that the Ghose–Patra seven-valued logic is a finite Heyting algebra, without giving an order or operations. It proposes that a quantum potential scaled by 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1 (λ = 1 quantum, λ = 0 classical Hamilton–Jacobi) carries the presheaf continuously to a sheaf, which is asserted, not modelled. Its one worked formula, v2's Čech "obstruction class" [δs], is a coboundary and so is zero by construction. | Rejected — read in full 2026-09-27 ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)); not worth a reader's time for its formal claims. What the essay adds is either unconstructed (the sheafification, the site, the seven-element Heyting algebra, the link from λ to cohomology) or wrong as stated: v2's obstruction class is zero by construction, a sheaf topos is not in general Boolean, and classical distributions do not form a sheaf. It gives the exact definition (a relative Čech class, with coefficients the free abelian group on support sections), the vanishing criterion and its two known failures. Its results are small propositions with complete proofs, plus machine-checked mod-2 computations that I reproduced. It calls itself "work in progress" (§1), and the conceptual development is in Abramsky et al.'s CSL 2015 "Contextuality, Cohomology and Paradox" (not read). For a model whose outcomes live in a commutative ring R, "All-vs-Nothing" (AvN_R) means the R-linear equations satisfied by every support section of every context have no global solution. A state ρ yields the sieve-valued valuation ν^ρ_V(P̂) = {V′ ⊆ V \| ρ(G(P̂)) = 1} (Def. 3.4) and the support projectors inf{P̂ ∈ L(V) \| ρ(P̂) = 1}. These form a global element of G and hence an "interval valuation", a subobject of Σ (§§4.2–4.4). The probability-r valuations give subobjects of G but not global elements. | Superseded — by [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md); read in full 2026-10-01 ([NOTE-327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-327.md)); covered better by part IV (Butterfield & Isham 2002, read alongside), which restates this paper's V-framework definitions nearly verbatim, proves the G ≅ CloΣ isomorphism that this paper only asserts and develops its interval valuations into theorems, and by Döring–Isham II ([LIT-335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md)), whose spectral presheaf over V(H) and clopen propositions are the mature form; it remains the citation for introducing V as the base category (as [LIT-335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md) credits it). |
| [LIT-381](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-381.md) v2 | A Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: II. Conceptual Aspects, and Classical Analogues | Butterfield & Isham (1998), arXiv:quant-ph/9808067. Butterfield & Isham argue that the sieve-valued "generalised valuations" of part I are not a quantum peculiarity but the natural valuations for any presheaf of propositions on any small category. Three supports are offered. (1) Classical physics: the value presheaf Υ(Ā) = Ā(S) on the category M of measurable functions has global sections (one per microstate, eq. 3.7), yet a macrostate R ⊆ S yields a sieve-valued valuation ν^R(A ∈ Δ) = {f_M \| B̄(R) ⊆ f(Δ)} (eq. 3.10) with the same FUNC property as the quantum ν^ρ. (2) A proof that a sieve-valued valuation on any presheaf G obeys generalised FUNC, ν(B, G(f)(d)) = f*(ν(A, d)), iff it is a natural transformation G → Ω, i.e. a subobject of G (Theorem 4.1). (3) An informal argument, explicitly "not a genuine deduction" (§5.2), that if partial truth is fixed by which weakenings of a proposition are totally true, the truth value is a sieve. | Active — read in full 2026-10-01 ([NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md)); worth reading as the series' conceptual companion and the only place it states the classical analogue and the partial-truth motivation; the mathematics is light (one short theorem), and the sieve semantics it motivates is carried on in part III, part IV and Döring–Isham ([LIT-343](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-343.md), [LIT-335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-335.md)). |
| [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md) v2 | A Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: IV. Interval Valuations | Butterfield & Isham (2001), arXiv:quant-ph/0107123. Butterfield & Isham show, over the poset V of commutative von Neumann subalgebras, that sieve-valued valuations and "interval valuations" (assignments of support projectors, or of subsets of Gelfand spectra) determine each other under stated conditions. If supports s(α, V) = inf{P̂ \| α_V(P̂) = true_V} form a global element of the coarse-graining presheaf G, then α_{V₁}(P̂) = {V₂ ⊆ V₁ \| G(s(α, V₁)) ≤ G(P̂)} is a sieve-valued valuation obeying FUNC (Theorem 3.1). There is an analogue for "tight" subobjects of Σ (Theorem 3.2). Both are satisfied by every state's valuation ν^ρ. The ordering ≤ (or ⊆) is shown to be the natural relation securing sievehood, null, monotonicity, exclusivity and unit (§4). The review §2.4 also supplies the proof, via state extension, that G ≅ CloΣ: restricting the clopen set of P̂ to V₂ gives the clopen set of its coarse-graining. Part III had only asserted this. | Active — read in full 2026-10-01 ([NOTE-328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-328.md)); worth reading as the finished statement of the series' von Neumann-algebra framework. It proves the G ≅ CloΣ isomorphism (coarse-graining = direct image of clopen regions) that Döring–Isham's daseinisation relies on, and it shows that a state's sieve-valued truth values are fixed by its support, a global element of G. Its two theorems are correct but close to definitional, so its value lies in the framework rather than in depth. |
| [LIT-389](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) v2 | Some Possible Roles for Topos Theory in Quantum Theory and Quantum Gravity | Isham & Butterfield (1999), arXiv:gr-qc/9910005. Isham & Butterfield argue, without proving anything new, that presheaf toposes over a base of "contexts" suit physics because the subobject classifier Ω is fixed by the base. They say this answers the objection that many-valued logics are arbitrary (§2.2), and that it keeps the logic distributive (§1.1). They then sketch seven applications. Five are speculative one-paragraph proposals (frames, observers, causal sets, TQFT, synthetic-differential-geometry time in continuous histories). One (§3.7) recaps their Kochen–Specker results: KS ⇔ the dual presheaf D(Â) = Hom(W_A, {0,1}) on the operator category O has no global sections (dim H > 2), and every state ψ gives a FUNC-obeying sieve-valued valuation ν^ψ(A ∈ Δ) = {f_O : Â → B̂ \| Ê[B ∈ f(Δ)]ψ = ψ}. | Active — read in full 2026-10-01 ([NOTE-334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-334.md)); worth reading only as the programme's short, informal manifesto as of 1999, written before parts III–IV appeared. It joins the Kochen–Specker valuations to the continuum scepticism (real-valued quantities, space and probabilities) that the Döring–Isham programme later develops, and the Literalism/Extra-Values framing appears nowhere else in the record. Its one technical section is a recap of KS I–II, and a reader of [LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md), [LIT-381](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-381.md) and [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) loses little by skipping it. |
| [LIT-390](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-390.md) v2 | Topos Theory and Consistent Histories: The Internal Logic of the Set of All Consistent Sets | Isham (1996), arXiv:gr-qc/9607069. Isham takes the poset B of all Boolean subalgebras ("windows") of the history orthoalgebra UP, ordered by coarse-graining, and shows that the presheaf A_d(W) = {α \| some d-consistent W′ ⊇ W contains α} is a subobject of the constant presheaf ΔUP, whereas the naive "realisable in W" assignment is not a presheaf at all (§4.1–4.2). The probability claim ⟨α, p⟩ then gets the sieve-valued semantic value {W ⊆ W₀ \| ∃ d-consistent W′ ⊇ W with α ∈ W′} if d(α, α) = p and ∅ otherwise (4.16), a global element 1 → Ω in Set^B, so the logic of "all consistent sets at once" is the distributive but non-Boolean Heyting algebra of sieves on B. | Active — read in full 2026-10-01 ([NOTE-333](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-333.md)); worth reading as the origin of the Isham school's sieve-valued, coarse-graining truth values, which the Kochen–Specker series names as its motivation (KS I, ref. [13]); it is the only place the construction is applied to consistent histories, it is short and elementary, and its constructions are correct as stated, but read it knowing that the Heyting values measure only whether α can be embedded in a consistent set (the probability d(α, α) is the same in every window), so it says nothing about the conflicts between consistent sets that motivate it. |
| [LIT-441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-441.md) | The Conscious Mind: In Search of a Fundamental Theory | Chalmers (1996), Oxford University Press. Per its introduction, the book argues that consciousness cannot be reductively explained and that materialism is false, and then moves toward a nonreductive theory with fundamental psychophysical laws. Its contents run from supervenience and explanation through the irreducibility argument, naturalistic dualism and the paradox of phenomenal judgment, to coherence principles, absent, fading and dancing qualia, and information. It ends with a defence of strong AI and a no-collapse reading of quantum mechanics. Unread: registered from the author's posted contents, introduction and jacket copy. | Deferred — registered 2026-10-02 from the author's posted table of contents, introduction and jacket copy, not read: no lawful full text could be reached. The author posts only those three, not draft chapters. Its two central arguments for this record are readable in their paper versions, [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md) (the hard problem and naturalistic dualism) and [LIT-392](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-392.md) (chapter 7's organizational invariance). It stays Deferred until a copy is supplied. |
